summary: Record the first executable controller skeleton as a cross-cutting behavioral implementation change requiring full five-stage review before further implementation proceeds.
reason: The skeleton establishes controller-owned state invariants, canonical stage ordering, identity types, machine-readable outcome/error semantics, and the persistence protocol consumed by later implementation. These decisions materially span adversarial failure/replay safety, inter-module authority and propagation, normalization of identities/status/error vocabulary, structural decomposition, and end-to-end lifecycle/recovery behavior. Implementation must therefore stop at commit 194339a7d27a5d14eead71e316101916992d9a45 and complete the full governed review before the in-memory backend or later layers are added.

reasons: This execution unit covers only the Adversarial stage of the frozen controller-core skeleton; the other four semantic stages remain separate later execution units.
The governed implementation surface is small and cohesive enough to test failure, replay, authority-bypass, mutation, stale-state, and representability risks in one bounded Adversarial pass.

workload.notes: Revision-1 full-program Adversarial stage under SEPARATED execution; no semantic stage credit is created by this gate.

capability.benchmark_evidence: Built-in separated default; not a claim of measured reviewer capability.

decision.assurance_boundary: Semantic judgment determines whether one pass is suitable and which bounded subpasses require isolation. Deterministic policy defaults to SEPARATED, converts declared isolation requirements into ISOLATED subpasses, and permits FUSED only through exact pre-existing VALIDATED capability permission. The gate and completion validator enforce the recorded plan but do not prove the semantic assessment itself was correct.

findings: BLOCKING: StateSnapshot permits terminal COMPLETE or FAILED states with a non-null open_occurrence_id, even though Phase-1 completion/failure semantics require the active occurrence to be closed or otherwise resolved before terminal state. This allows an internally contradictory authoritative state to be represented and handed to persistence.

BLOCKING: StateSnapshot review_revision validation only checks review_revision < 0. Python bool values therefore pass (True behaves as 1, False as 0), and other non-int comparable values may pass, violating the frozen requirement for a strict nonnegative integer revision identity and creating identity/canonicalization ambiguity.

BLOCKING: PersistenceBackend splits authoritative state and immutable history across read() and read_immutable_history(). The frozen controller contract requires one coherent authoritative read containing the state plus the immutable evidence needed for integrity and exact-retry decisions. Separate reads can observe different persistence moments under concurrency or recovery, producing torn retry/integrity decisions.

BLOCKING: ErrorCode omits an explicit commit-outcome-unknown/integrity outcome even though the frozen implementation plan requires machine-readable handling of ambiguous persistence commit results and integrity failures. Collapsing those cases into persistence_unavailable/conflict would make crash-after-commit recovery and retry semantics unsafe or ambiguous.

NON-BLOCKING/DEFER: ProgramState.DRAFT remains publicly constructible through StateSnapshot. The frozen Phase-1 contract reserves draft as non-constructible in Phase-1 operations. Because the initialization/controller path has not yet been implemented, this must be explicitly prevented by that path or tightened in domain construction before conformance credit; it is not independently the primary blocker while the above state and persistence defects remain.
evidence: Issue #10 frozen execution contract and draft clarification
unresolved_conditions: Do not advance to Interdependency. Correct the blocking domain-state, strict revision-typing, coherent-read, and persistence outcome taxonomy defects; record the behavioral corrections; regenerate the queue; increment review_revision and reopen Adversarial against the corrected governed target.

After correction, add focused regression coverage for terminal/open-occurrence contradiction, bool/non-int review revisions, coherent persistence read semantics, and ambiguous commit/integrity outcome taxonomy.
DRAFT non-constructibility must be mechanically enforced by the Phase-1 initialization/controller path or by domain validation before Phase-1 implementation is credited.
